methodology.strands.heading: Three branches, five strands, one reading child.
methodology.strands.body: LCS is the shape of a whole language education, not a list of subjects. Literacy is where language goes in. Composition is where it comes back out, in an order that holds. Speaking is the part a book cannot do for you. Five content strands sit under those branches, and more than one of them is running in any given session even when only one has your child’s attention.
methodology.strands.L.body: The reading treasury — where language goes in, and the root of everything a child later writes or says.
methodology.strands.L.nested.0.name: Literature
methodology.strands.L.nested.0.body: Whole, unabridged classics, read for craft. Not excerpts and not retellings — the sentences the writer actually wrote, at the length they wrote them.
methodology.strands.L.nested.1.name: Vocabulary
methodology.strands.L.nested.1.body: The Latin and Greek roots beneath English. Structure rather than memorization, so a word your child has never met becomes one they can take apart.
methodology.strands.L.nested.2.name: Poetics
methodology.strands.L.nested.2.body: The ear for how good writing is built — rhythm, image, the choice a writer made and the one they turned down.
methodology.strands.C.body: The construction engine — where language comes out, and where thinking has to survive being written down.
methodology.strands.C.nested.0.name: Grammar
methodology.strands.C.nested.0.body: The architecture of the sentence, taught first and taught quickly, then used rather than recited.
methodology.strands.C.nested.1.name: Writing
methodology.strands.C.nested.1.body: Sentence to paragraph to essay to academic composition, each step assessed before the next one is asked for.
methodology.strands.S.body: DODO’s own strand, and the reason there is a Navigator in the room at all. Oral defence, Socratic dialogue, taking the side you disagree with. It has no nested strand because nothing in a curriculum of books supplies it.
methodology.strands.note: Read → Think → Speak → Write is how one session runs. The strands are what the sessions are made of.
methodology.research.heading: The part of this you can go and check.
methodology.research.body: English is built out of Latin and Greek — about sixty percent of it, and over ninety percent of the language of science. We teach the roots beneath the words, so a term your child has never seen becomes one they can take apart and solve. It happens to be one of the most-researched strategies in education, which means you do not have to take our word for any of it.
methodology.research.findings.0.claim: In a study of 493 middle-school students, root-based vocabulary teaching outperformed memorization — for gifted and typically-developing students alike.
methodology.research.findings.1.claim: Across dozens of controlled studies, teaching the structure of words produces measurable gains in vocabulary, decoding and spelling.
methodology.research.findings.2.claim: The gains are largest when word structure is woven into real reading rather than drilled on its own — which is why it lives inside the literature here, not beside it.
methodology.research.findings.3.claim: Children grow most on rich, challenging text rather than simplified readers. That is why we read real, unabridged classics, set a step above the comfortable level on purpose.
methodology.research.note: Roots are the reason the vocabulary transfers. A child who knows spect reads their way into inspect, circumspect, spectrum and spectacle without being taught a single one of them.
methodology.sessionTypes.heading: Every cycle runs two kinds of session.
methodology.sessionTypes.note: Which kind your child gets in a given week follows their current Lexile data, not a fixed rotation. If the reading needs another week, it gets another week.
program.architecture.body: The LCS System — Literacy · Composition · Speaking — is the curriculum architecture. Five content strands nest under those three branches. Within it, every session runs The Loop, guided by your child’s Navigator. Across each 16-week cycle, sessions accumulate into LCS strand progress. Across multiple cycles, students advance through the seven ELA levels (Levels 1–7), with Level 7 reaching college-tier academic English. Each level takes two to three cycles. Each cycle is 16 weeks.
program.architecture.S.nestedNote: DODO’s own strand — no nested strand, because no book supplies it.
compare.s3.h2: Five comparisons that clarify what DODO Learning actually is.
compare.s3.cols.0.title: Cognitive development — not language practice
compare.s3.cols.0.body: Tutoring centres fix homework. ESL programs build conversational fluency. DODO Learning develops the reasoning architecture that makes your child capable of reading dense analytical prose, arguing a position with textual evidence, and writing with precision. It is a different category of work, and it produces a different kind of student.
compare.s3.cols.1.title: Measured against their own ceiling
compare.s3.cols.2.title: A sixteen-week arc
compare.s3.cols.3.question: vs. AI tutors and homework apps
compare.s3.cols.3.title: The judgment behind the question
compare.s3.cols.3.body: AI is a tool your child will use for the rest of their life, and using it well is a skill worth having. What it cannot do is build the judgment underneath. It will answer whatever it is asked. A Navigator teaches your child which question is worth asking, then presses on the point they have not made yet — and the reading and the reasoning stay your child’s own work.
compare.s3.cols.4.question: vs. buying the curriculum yourself
compare.s3.cols.4.title: A live reader in the room
compare.s3.cols.4.body: The classical ELA materials are real books, and a determined family can buy them. What arrives is the reading and the writing. What cannot arrive is the third strand — someone who hears how your child reasons, asks the harder question at the moment it would land, and coaches the spoken defence of an idea. That part has no page.
compare.s4.h2: What separates DODO Learning is the LCS System.
compare.s4.caption: Inside every session the same sequence runs: Read → Think → Speak → Write. Each stage is assessed, and each one feeds the next. Over sixteen weeks a child working this way with a Navigator does not only read better. They get better at working through anything difficult, which is the part that keeps paying.
compare.s5.sub: Eight unscripted minutes on why we started, and what we decided we would never do.
compare.s6.h2: What a Navigator does that a tutor cannot.
compare.s6.points.1.label: A better question
compare.s6.points.2.label: Feedback with a number attached
compare.s6.points.3.body: Your child’s Navigator is with them from initial Lexile assessment to final 6+1 Trait evaluation. One relationship, one standard, and the same set of eyes on every draft and every oral defence your child gives. The relationship itself is part of the program.
compare.s7.cols.0.title: A Lexile number
compare.s7.cols.1.title: Seven traits, scored
compare.s7.cols.2.title: A cycle with a beginning and an end
compare.s7.cols.2.body: The ELA Program has a beginning, a measurable midpoint, and a confirmed result. It is not a monthly subscription you drift in and out of, because the compounding only happens when the work is continuous and the Navigator’s knowledge of your child keeps accumulating.
